findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The suffix-matching logic in website_name treats any two hosts sharing the same public-suffix tail (e.g. a forum at forums.example.co.uk and a website at somethingelse.co.uk, both 4 labels with suffix 'co.uk') as 'same site' and exposes the full host+path. Users on multi-level-TLD deployments (co.uk, com.au) get an unrelated external site rendered as if it were part of the instance, showing a longer URL than intended and mislabeling third-party links as internal; the existing spec cases (example.com, forums.example.com) never exercise this branch with multi-label public suffixes.

[ADVISORY] For a website value without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/profile'), URI(...).host is nil, so website_name returns nil and the template's {{#if model.website_name}} hides the link entirely, whereas the removed controller helper websiteName (split('/')[2]) displayed 'example.com' for the same value. Users whose saved profile website lacks a scheme lose their displayed website link after this change; whether such values can exist depends on upstream validation of user_profile.website, which the diff does not account for.

[BUG] website_name returns nil for websites stored without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user'), so the profile globe/link silently disappears for users whose website field lacks http:// URI('example.com/user').host returns nil, so website_host is nil and the method returns nil while website itself is present and rendered as an href — the template's {{#if model.website_name}} block hides the entry entirely, a regression from the old client-side websiteName which split on '/' and always produced the middle segment; users who entered bare domains lose the displayed website name

[ADVISORY] The www.example.com == forum.example.com branch (the elsif requiring equal segment counts > 2) is the only one of the three matching strategies with no test coverage in the new specs The added spec covers same-host, parent-host, and unmatched cases but never exercises the elsif branch (e.g. Discourse.current_hostname 'discourse.org' with website 'http://www.example.com'), so a regression in that segment-count logic — the most convoluted of the three — ships undetected; future refactors of the domain comparison are unprotected exactly where the logic is hardest to reason about

[ADVISORY] The elsif branch compares sibling subdomains but requires only discourse_host (not website_host) to have more than 2 segments, so a 3-segment website host against a 2-segment instance host falls to the ends_with? branch and gets path-appended when it is a subdomain of the website, an asymmetric result With instance host 'discourse.org' and website 'http://www.discourse.org/x', website_host has 3 segments vs discourse_host's 2, so the elsif is skipped; the else branch finds 'discourse.org'.ends_with?('.www.discourse.org') false and returns bare 'www.discourse.org' — but with website 'http://forum.discourse.org/x' the ends_with? succeeds and 'forum.discourse.org/x' is shown, so sibling subdomains of the instance are treated inconsistently depending on which side is the subdomain; the mismatch is invisible because no test exercises either permutation

[BUG] The client-side `websiteName` computed property is deleted here, but only templates/controllers/user.hbs is migrated to `model.website_name`; the user card template (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/card.hbs) also renders the user's website using `websiteName`, so the card view loses its website display name binding after this change. On the user card popover, the website link renders an empty/undefined label where the hostname previously appeared, for every user with a website set, because the property it references no longer exists on the controller.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated doc-comment edit renaming `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground` is bundled into this PR and is not traceable to the stated requirement of showing the full URL path for same-domain websites. The comment change silently fixes a pre-existing doc drift in the same file; harmless functionally, but it is scope creep that muddies review attribution and would be better as its own commit.

[ADVISORY] The `www.example.com == forum.example.com` branch (equal label counts > 2, suffix match on labels [1..-1]) has no test coverage in the added spec, which only exercises same-host, different-host, and parent-domain cases. The branch handling both hosts being siblings under a shared registrable domain (e.g. website `www.example.com` on instance `forum.example.com`, which is exactly the case the PR is about) can regress silently; a future refactor that misindexes `split('.')[1..-1]` ships untested.

[BUG] The label-count/suffix heuristic treats any two hosts sharing the same trailing labels as the same site, so unrelated domains on multi-part public suffixes are treated as same-domain and the full URL path is exposed. With Discourse.current_hostname = 'www.discourse.co.uk' and a user website of 'http://evil.co.uk/private/photos', both hosts split into 3 labels and split('.')[1..-1].join('.') yields 'co.uk' == 'co.uk', so website_name returns 'evil.co.uk/private/photos' — the full path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text, contrary to the feature's intent of revealing the path only for the instance's own domain.

[BUG] The template condition switched from a controller-computed name to model.website_name, so for a website value whose URI parse yields no host, the entire website link silently disappears instead of rendering as before. For a user_profile.website like 'example.com/user' (no scheme), URI(website).host is nil, website_name returns nil while include_website_name's website.present? passes; {{#if model.website_name}} is false, so users who previously saw a globe link (old code rendered website.split("/")[2] = 'example.com') now see nothing — a sentinel-meaning change where a present website now renders as absent.

[ADVISORY] Same-site detection misses the case where the website is a subdomain of the instance domain (instance 'example.com', website 'www.example.com'): label counts differ (2 vs 3) and the else branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?(website_host), so it returns bare 'www.example.com' without the path. A user whose personal site is a subdomain of the forum's own domain — the clearest same-site case — gets the truncated host-only display the feature was meant to fix, producing inconsistent behavior depending on which side holds the subdomain.

[ADVISORY] URI(website.to_s) is parsed up to three times per website_name call, with the second parse relying on the first having succeeded even though each has its own rescue-free failure point. If the first parse succeeds but a second raises (currently impossible for the same string, but the duplication means a refactor of one copy silently diverges from the others); the three-way if/elsif/else with repeated host/path extraction should parse once into variables and dispatch on a small helper, keeping the host-comparison rules in one place for the next rule addition.

[BUG] The suffix-equality matching in website_name treats any shared trailing labels as 'same domain', so distinct sites like foo.co.uk vs bar.co.uk (or evilwww.example.com vs www.example.com in the elsif branch) match and the full untrusted URL path is displayed as if it were the instance's own domain. A user sets website to http://foo.co.uk/ while the instance runs at bar.co.uk (or http://evilwww.example.com/ while instance is www.example.com); website_name renders 'foo.co.uk/anything' — the display the PR reserves for same-instance links is shown for an unrelated third-party host, defeating the stated intent 'show complete path if website domain is same as instance domain' and creating a look-alike trust signal.

[ADVISORY] website_name duplicates Discourse.current_hostname.split('.') three times and hand-rolls three near-identical host+path concatenations instead of computing the match once and returning in a single place. The next change to the matching rule (e.g. fixing the suffix bug above) must be edited consistently in three branches plus their comments; a missed branch silently produces inconsistent website_name values for structurally identical inputs, and this is exactly where the foo.co.uk/evilwww conflation already slipped through.

[ADVISORY] URI(website).path is appended verbatim, so 'http://example.com/' serializes website_name as 'example.com/' with a dangling trailing slash. Every user whose website URL has a bare trailing slash and matches the instance domain gets a visibly truncated-slash label in their profile header; cosmetic but visible to all profile viewers on every page load.

[ADVISORY] Rendering the attacker-controlled URI path of a user's website field alongside the trusted instance hostname enables in-domain spoofing of official-looking links/paths on the profile card. Any user can set their website to a URL on the instance's own domain (e.g. https://<instance>/u/admin or a plausible internal path) and the profile now displays the full path next to the instance's hostname, lending forged context to phishing/social-engineering inside the site (HTML escaping in the template prevents script injection, so this is deception, not XSS).

[ADVISORY] The new website_name tests cover only three of the serializer's four branches, leaving the equal-segment-count subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) and its negative case (different subdomains -> bare host) untested. A regression in the `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` branch of app/serializers/user_serializer.rb (e.g. an off-by-one in the [1..-1] slice or the > 2 guard) passes the suite silently, so users with www-style sites get a wrong display name with no test failure.

[ADVISORY] The rescue-nil on URI parsing means a malformed website value yields nil while include_website_name still includes the key, and this path has no test in the diff. A user profile with a non-URL website string (e.g. 'not a url') serializes website_name as null next to the raw website string; the frontend {{#if model.website_name}} hides the link entirely, and no test in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb exercises the malformed-input path, so a future refactor of the rescue (e.g. dropping it) would raise URI::InvalidURIError in the serializer for every user card render without a failing test.

[ADVISORY] website_name compares hosts case-sensitively, so a website URL like 'http://WWW.Example.com/user' on an instance with hostname 'www.example.com' misses the equality branch and silently drops the path, rendering only the host. Users whose website field differs only in case see the truncated host-only label even though the PR's stated goal is showing the full path for same-domain sites; every case variant hits the fallback branch.

[ADVISORY] The same-domain comparison ignores the URL port, so 'http://example.com:8080/user' has website_host 'example.com' matching the equality branch but a non-matching instance still falls through; conversely on an instance at a nonstandard port the equality check compares hostname only and works, but a website on 'example.com:8080' with instance 'example.com' takes the equality branch yet the elsif/else label-count heuristics treat ports inconsistently across branches. Websites saved with explicit ports (a form Discourse accepts) get the host-only fallback and the path is dropped, contradicting the feature's intent for exactly the same-site case it targets.

[ADVISORY] URI(website.to_s) is parsed up to three times per serialized user (once with rescue nil, once per matching branch path), re-doing the same parse that already succeeded. The serializer runs on every user card/profile payload; the redundant parses are wasted work on a hot path and the second/third parses are only safe because the first happened to succeed, a coupling that breaks silently if the two call sites ever diverge (e.g. one gains normalization).

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the only cases that return `website_host + path` are (a) `website_host == discourse_host`, (b) the “same length” branch where all labels except the first match (`website_host.split('.')[1..] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..]`), or (c) when the instance host ends with `"." + website_host` (website is a parent domain of the instance). None of these conditions would treat unrelated hosts that merely share a public-suffix tail (e.g., `forums.example.co.uk` vs `somethingelse.co.uk`) as the same site: label counts differ so it falls to the `ends_with?` check, which will be false, and returns only `website_host` (no path). While the tests don’t cover multi-label TLDs, the specific misclassification described is not supported by the diff’s logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] For a website value without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/profile'), URI(...).host is nil, so website_name returns nil and the template's {{#if model.website_name}} hides the link entirely, whereas the removed controller helper websiteName (split('/')[2]) displayed 'example.com' for the same value. Users whose saved profile website lacks a scheme lose their displayed website link after this change; whether such values can exist depends on upstream validation of user_profile.website, which the diff does not account for.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the removed controller helper `websiteName` would display `example.com` for a scheme-less value like `example.com/profile`, but the old implementation `website.split("/")[2]` would return `nil` for that input (it only returns a host when the string contains a scheme like `http://...`). Therefore, the link would also have been hidden previously. While the new serializer method `website_name` does return `nil` when `URI(...).host` is nil, the diff does not show a behavioral regression for the specific scheme-less example given.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] website_name returns nil for websites stored without a scheme (e.g. 'example.com/user'), so the profile globe/link silently disappears for users whose website field lacks http:// URI('example.com/user').host returns nil, so website_host is nil and the method returns nil while website itself is present and rendered as an href — the template's {{#if model.website_name}} block hides the entry entirely, a regression from the old client-side websiteName which split on '/' and always produced the middle segment; users who entered bare domains lose the displayed website name

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` derives `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host` and returns early if `website_host` is nil. For a value like `example.com/user` (no scheme), Ruby's `URI()` treats it as a path and `.host` is nil, so `website_name` becomes nil even though `include_website_name` includes the attribute when `website.present?`. Since the template now guards display with `{{#if model.website_name}}`, a scheme-less website would not render the globe/link. However, the finding's claim that the old client-side `websiteName` "always" produced a name is not supported by the removed code (it also relied on `split('/')[2]`, which would be nil for `example.com/user`). Whether scheme-less values can actually be stored isn't verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The www.example.com == forum.example.com branch (the elsif requiring equal segment counts > 2) is the only one of the three matching strategies with no test coverage in the new specs The added spec covers same-host, parent-host, and unmatched cases but never exercises the elsif branch (e.g. Discourse.current_hostname 'discourse.org' with website 'http://www.example.com'), so a regression in that segment-count logic — the most convoluted of the three — ships undetected; future refactors of the domain comparison are unprotected exactly where the logic is hardest to reason about

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name` with three distinct match strategies: `website_host == discourse_host`, an `elsif` for equal segment counts > 2 with parent-domain comparison, and an `else` using `ends_with?`. The new specs cover the first branch (same host: `current_hostname 'example.com'`) and the `else` branch (parent-host: `current_hostname 'forums.example.com'` with `website_host 'example.com'`) plus an unmatched case (`'discourse.org'` vs `'example.com'`). None of the tests exercise the `elsif` path where both hosts have >2 segments and equal segment counts (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), so regressions in that specific logic would be untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The elsif branch compares sibling subdomains but requires only discourse_host (not website_host) to have more than 2 segments, so a 3-segment website host against a 2-segment instance host falls to the ends_with? branch and gets path-appended when it is a subdomain of the website, an asymmetric result With instance host 'discourse.org' and website 'http://www.discourse.org/x', website_host has 3 segments vs discourse_host's 2, so the elsif is skipped; the else branch finds 'discourse.org'.ends_with?('.www.discourse.org') false and returns bare 'www.discourse.org' — but with website 'http://forum.discourse.org/x' the ends_with? succeeds and 'forum.discourse.org/x' is shown, so sibling subdomains of the instance are treated inconsistently depending on which side is the subdomain; the mismatch is invisible because no test exercises either permutation

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb` is indeed asymmetric: it appends the path when `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` (i.e., when the *instance* is a subdomain of the website host), but not when the website host is a subdomain of the instance host. Also, the `elsif` only considers the “sibling subdomain” case when `discourse_host.split('.').length > 2`, so cases like instance `discourse.org` vs website `www.discourse.org` are handled by the `else` and will return just `www.discourse.org` (no path). The specific claim that the `ends_with?` check would succeed for instance `discourse.org` and website `forum.discourse.org` is incorrect (it would be false), but the broader point stands: there is an untested, nontrivial edge-case/permutation in this newly added branching logic, and the spec only covers website parent-of-instance, not the reverse.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The client-side `websiteName` computed property is deleted here, but only templates/controllers/user.hbs is migrated to `model.website_name`; the user card template (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/user/card.hbs) also renders the user's website using `websiteName`, so the card view loses its website display name binding after this change. adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `websiteName` computed property from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name`, but it does not include `templates/user/card.hbs` (or any other template) to confirm it still references `websiteName`. Since the alleged breakage depends on an unchanged reference in a file not shown in the diff, the finding cannot be verified from the provided changes alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes an unrelated documentation-only change in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/user.js.es6` updating the doc comment from `@property websiteName` to `@property profileBackground`. This is not required for the main functional change (moving `websiteName` logic from the controller/template to `website_name` in the serializer) and is effectively a separate cleanup, i.e., scope creep that can muddy review attribution, but it does not introduce a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `www.example.com == forum.example.com` branch (equal label counts > 2, suffix match on labels [1..-1]) has no test coverage in the added spec, which only exercises same-host, different-host, and parent-domain cases. adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the new `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch handles sibling subdomains (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) by comparing `split('.')[1..-1]` and conditionally returning `website_host + URI(...).path`. The added specs only cover: different-host (`discourse.org`), same-host (`example.com`), and parent-domain (`forums.example.com` with `example.com` website). There is no spec that sets `current_hostname` to a sibling subdomain with equal label count (e.g. `forum.example.com`) and website to another sibling (e.g. `www.example.com`), so that branch can regress without failing tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The label-count/suffix heuristic treats any two hosts sharing the same trailing labels as the same site, so unrelated domains on multi-part public suffixes are treated as same-domain and the full URL path is exposed. With Discourse.current_hostname = 'www.discourse.co.uk' and a user website of 'http://evil.co.uk/private/photos', both hosts split into 3 labels and split('.')[1..-1].join('.') yields 'co.uk' == 'co.uk', so website_name returns 'evil.co.uk/private/photos' — the full path of an unrelated third-party site is rendered as the link text, contrary to the feature's intent of revealing the path only for the instance's own domain.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif` branch treats two hosts as related when they have the same number of dot-labels (>2) and the tail labels (everything except the first label) match: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(...).path : website_host`. This will incorrectly consider unrelated domains under a multi-part public suffix (e.g., `forums.co.uk` vs `evil.co.uk`) as “same site” because both tails become `co.uk`, causing it to return `website_host + path` and thus expose/render the full path for an unrelated third-party domain. The finding’s specific example uses `www.discourse.co.uk` (4 labels) vs `evil.co.uk` (3 labels), so that exact condition wouldn’t trigger, but the underlying defect in the heuristic is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The template condition switched from a controller-computed name to model.website_name, so for a website value whose URI parse yields no host, the entire website link silently disappears instead of rendering as before. For a user_profile.website like 'example.com/user' (no scheme), URI(website).host is nil, website_name returns nil while include_website_name's website.present? passes; {{#if model.website_name}} is false, so users who previously saw a globe link (old code rendered website.split("/")[2] = 'example.com') now see nothing — a sentinel-meaning change where a present website now renders as absent.

adjudication.rationale: The claimed regression for a scheme-less website like 'example.com/user' is not supported by the diff: the old Ember `websiteName` computed used `website.split("/")[2]`, which would be `nil` for 'example.com/user' (array has only 2 elements), so `{{#if websiteName}}` would also have been false and the globe/link would not render. The new behavior (URI host nil => `website_name` nil => `{{#if model.website_name}}` false) matches that old outcome, so the finding’s “previously rendered 'example.com'” assertion is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Same-site detection misses the case where the website is a subdomain of the instance domain (instance 'example.com', website 'www.example.com'): label counts differ (2 vs 3) and the else branch only checks discourse_host.ends_with?(website_host), so it returns bare 'www.example.com' without the path. A user whose personal site is a subdomain of the forum's own domain — the clearest same-site case — gets the truncated host-only display the feature was meant to fix, producing inconsistent behavior depending on which side holds the subdomain.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the “include path” conditions cover (a) exact host match and (b) instance host being a subdomain of the website host via `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)`. The reverse relationship (website host being a subdomain of the instance host, e.g. instance `example.com`, website `www.example.com`) is not handled, so it will fall through to returning just `website_host` (no path). This is a concrete, diff-grounded edge case omission, but it’s not clearly a verifiable defect from the diff alone because the intended semantics for subdomain websites aren’t specified or tested here.

adjudication.rationale: In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, the code calls `URI(website.to_s)` once to get `host` (with `rescue nil`) and then calls `URI(website.to_s).path` again in multiple branches without rescue. This is diff-grounded duplication that adds unnecessary parsing and increases maintenance risk if one callsite is changed later. It’s not a correctness bug as shown, but a concrete refactor/robustness concern introduced by the new method.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the `elsif` branch treats any two hosts with the same label count (>2) and identical trailing labels (after dropping the first label) as equivalent: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1].join('.') ? website_host + URI(...).path : website_host`. This will incorrectly classify `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` as “same domain” because both reduce to `co.uk`, causing the full path to be displayed (`foo.co.uk/<path>`) even though they are unrelated registrable domains. The diff’s logic is therefore susceptible to public-suffix cases and matches the finding’s described behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/user_serializer.rb`, `website_name` repeats `discourse_host.split('.')` and its `length` multiple times in the `elsif` condition, and it also repeats the `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` concatenation in more than one branch. This is a diff-grounded maintainability concern (logic is harder to change consistently), but it is not itself a demonstrable correctness defect from the diff alone; the mention of a specific prior “suffix bug”/“foo.co.uk” issue is not verifiable here.

This is a real edge-case formatting/UI concern, but it’s cosmetic and not clearly an actual functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Rendering the attacker-controlled URI path of a user's website field alongside the trusted instance hostname enables in-domain spoofing of official-looking links/paths on the profile card. Any user can set their website to a URL on the instance's own domain (e.g. https://<instance>/u/admin or a plausible internal path) and the profile now displays the full path next to the instance's hostname, lending forged context to phishing/social-engineering inside the site (HTML escaping in the template prevents script injection, so this is deception, not XSS).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes profile display from showing only the website host (removed `websiteName` in `controllers/user.js.es6` which did `website.split("/")[2]`) to showing `model.website_name` computed server-side. In `user_serializer.rb#website_name`, when `website_host == Discourse.current_hostname` (or when the website domain is a parent of the instance domain), it returns `website_host + URI(...).path`, i.e. attacker-controlled path appended to the trusted instance hostname (e.g. `example.com/user`). The template (`user/user.hbs`) renders this string as the visible link text, enabling in-domain spoofing/social-engineering as described (even though HTML escaping prevents XSS).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new website_name tests cover only three of the serializer's four branches, leaving the equal-segment-count subdomain branch (www.example.com vs forum.example.com) and its negative case (different subdomains -> bare host) untested. A regression in the `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` branch of app/serializers/user_serializer.rb (e.g. an off-by-one in the [1..-1] slice or the > 2 guard) passes the suite silently, so users with www-style sites get a wrong display name with no test failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, there is a distinct `elsif (website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length) && discourse_host.split('.').length > 2` branch with a ternary that returns either `website_host + path` (when the stripped domains match) or just `website_host` (when they don’t). The added specs cover: (1) different unrelated domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`) hitting the final `else`, (2) exact same domain hitting the first `if`, and (3) parent-domain case (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`) also hitting the final `else`. No spec exercises the equal-segment-count branch (e.g., `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) nor its negative subcase, so regressions in that logic could slip through.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rescue-nil on URI parsing means a malformed website value yields nil while include_website_name still includes the key, and this path has no test in the diff. A user profile with a non-URL website string (e.g. 'not a url') serializes website_name as null next to the raw website string; the frontend {{#if model.website_name}} hides the link entirely, and no test in spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb exercises the malformed-input path, so a future refactor of the rescue (e.g. dropping it) would raise URI::InvalidURIError in the serializer for every user card render without a failing test.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, URI parsing is wrapped in `rescue nil` (`website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil`) and the method returns `nil` when `website_host` is `nil`. However `include_website_name` is based only on `website.present?`, so a non-empty but malformed `website` value would still include `website_name` in JSON as `null`. The added specs only cover valid URL cases and do not exercise the malformed-input/rescue path, so this nontrivial branch is untested as the finding notes. This is a test/edge-case coverage concern rather than a definite defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] website_name compares hosts case-sensitively, so a website URL like 'http://WWW.Example.com/user' on an instance with hostname 'www.example.com' misses the equality branch and silently drops the path, rendering only the host. Users whose website field differs only in case see the truncated host-only label even though the PR's stated goal is showing the full path for same-domain sites; every case variant hits the fallback branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `website_host` from `URI(...).host` is compared to `Discourse.current_hostname` using case-sensitive `==` and later case-sensitive string comparisons (`split`/`join` equality, `ends_with?`). Since DNS hostnames are case-insensitive, a URL like `http://WWW.Example.com/user` on an instance with `www.example.com` will miss the same-domain branches and fall through to returning just `website_host` (dropping the path), contrary to the intended behavior shown by the added tests for same-domain/path inclusion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The same-domain comparison ignores the URL port, so 'http://example.com:8080/user' has website_host 'example.com' matching the equality branch but a non-matching instance still falls through; conversely on an instance at a nonstandard port the equality check compares hostname only and works, but a website on 'example.com:8080' with instance 'example.com' takes the equality branch yet the elsif/else label-count heuristics treat ports inconsistently across branches. Websites saved with explicit ports (a form Discourse accepts) get the host-only fallback and the path is dropped, contradicting the feature's intent for exactly the same-site case it targets.

adjudication.rationale: In `website_name`, the code uses `URI(website.to_s).host`, which strips any port, and compares it to `Discourse.current_hostname` (also a hostname string in this diff). Even if the saved website URL includes an explicit port (e.g. `example.com:8080`), `website_host` becomes `example.com`, so the equality branch (or other hostname-based branches) will still return `website_host + URI(...).path` in the “same-site” cases—i.e., the path is not dropped as the finding claims. The diff shows no handling of ports at all, nor evidence that `current_hostname` includes a port, so the port-based fall-through/path-drop behavior described is not verifiable from this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] URI(website.to_s) is parsed up to three times per serialized user (once with rescue nil, once per matching branch path), re-doing the same parse that already succeeded. The serializer runs on every user card/profile payload; the redundant parses are wasted work on a hot path and the second/third parses are only safe because the first happened to succeed, a coupling that breaks silently if the two call sites ever diverge (e.g. one gains normalization).

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, `URI(website.to_s)` is invoked multiple times: once to get `.host` (`website_host = URI(...).host rescue nil`) and again in two branches to get `.path` (`website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`). This is redundant work per serialized user and also creates a mild maintainability coupling (future changes could affect one parse site but not the others). The diff shows no correctness break, just avoidable repeated parsing on a frequently executed serializer path.
